metadata.title: Robertson Bound on the Bloch Sphere — Zero Bound, Nonzero Uncertainty
metadata.purpose: Riff critique of the Robertson bound / actual sigma product D3 heatmap from QM vol 2

beats.narration_text: Konnichiwa. I'm Liam, in for Bear. This is the Robertson uncertainty bound visualized on the Bloch sphere — a D3 heat map that shows what happens to the uncertainty product as a quantum state moves from pole to equator. We are not judging the spin mechanics. We are judging the visualization.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for the Robertson uncertainty bound on the Bloch sphere.
output: ✓ Bloch sphere Mercator heatmap — φ/θ grid, RdBu color scale
✓ Robertson bound vs actual σ product, two commutator pairs

beats.narration_text: Two panels side by side. On the left, a Mercator projection of the Bloch sphere: azimuthal angle phi on the horizontal axis, polar angle theta on the vertical, colored from red at the poles to blue at the equatorial band. On the right, two curves over theta, fixed at phi equals forty-five degrees. Four toggle buttons switch between the Robertson bound and the actual sigma product, and between two commutator pairs. Click any cell and the tooltip reports both values.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B01.mp4 (output.mp4 full clip — baseline Robertson Bound heatmap)

beats.narration_text: The View toggle rewrites the heatmap. Robertson Bound mode: pure latitude stripes, no phi structure — the bound for the S-x S-y pair depends only on theta. Actual Sigma Product mode: four blue notches appear at the equator at phi equals zero, ninety, one-eighty, and two-seventy degrees. Those are the states where S-x or S-y has zero variance. Clicking a near-equatorial cell in Robertson Bound mode surfaces the key number: bound equals zero-point-zero-zero-seven, actual equals zero-point-one-two.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/B02.mp4 (change.mp4 full clip — interactive toggle + click-through)

beats.narration_text: Two things this visualization earns. First: the Mercator projection is the correct abstraction. The actual sigma product varies with phi — you cannot see that on a three-D sphere where perspective hides the azimuthal structure. The flat grid makes both axes scannable at once. Second: the click-to-inspect tooltip. It reports the Robertson bound and the actual value at any point and flags the critical case with the label: bound equals zero but actual not zero. The discrepancy is numerical, not inferred.
beats.new_visual_element: STILL: media/B03.png (change.mp4@9.0s — Actual σ Product view, butterfly φ-structure visible)

beats.narration_text: Two things the visualization hides. First: the static text card below the curve reads 'actual sigma S-x sigma S-y equals h-bar-squared over four everywhere.' That is wrong. The actual product depends on phi. At phi equals zero or ninety degrees it reaches zero at the equator. The heatmap in Actual Sigma mode shows this directly; the label contradicts it. The developer's own source comments document the error. Second: the curve panel locks phi at forty-five degrees with no control. That is the most informative slice, but a student cannot find the slice where bound and actual agree. The hardcoded choice teaches one case as if it were the whole story.
beats.new_visual_element: STILL: media/B04.png (output.mp4@1.0s — Robertson Bound default view, static text card visible)

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. The Mercator projection earns its keep — the phi structure in the actual sigma product is only visible in a two-D grid. The click tooltip delivers the discrepancy numerically. But two things need fixing: the static text card states h-bar-squared over four everywhere, which the heatmap itself disproves. And the curve panel locks phi at forty-five degrees with no control — the informative slice is the only slice, and that is not the complete picture.

props.artifactHeading: Robertson Bound on the Bloch Sphere
artifactLines: Mercator projection — right call; φ-structure only visible in a 2D grid
click-to-inspect tooltip — discrepancy is numerical, not inferred
static text claims ħ²/4 everywhere — the heatmap disproves this.
curve panel locks φ=45°; the φ=0° story is invisible

beats.narration_text: I have a D3 Bloch sphere visualization showing the Robertson uncertainty bound for spin-half. The right panel curve is hardcoded to phi equals forty-five degrees. Do two things: first, add a slider for phi from zero to three-sixty degrees that redraws the curve in real time, so viewers can explore when the actual product also reaches zero at the equator. Second, fix the static text below the curve: replace the claim that sigma-Sx sigma-Sy equals h-bar-squared over four everywhere with the correct formula — sigma-Sx sigma-Sy equals h-bar-squared over four, times the square root of one minus sin-squared theta cos-squared phi, times one minus sin-squared theta sin-squared phi. Keep the single-file D3 format.
